title: "Thus Shalt Thou Love the Almighty Lord
description: "Thus Shalt Thou Love the Almighty Lord in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Emily Taylor wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 341 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Thou shalt love the Lord thy God."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "Thus shalt thou love th'Al-might-y Lord, With all thy heart, and soul, and mind:" So speaks to man that sa-cred word, For coun-sel and re-proof de-signed.

lines: "Thus shalt thou love the Almighty Lord,
With all thy heart, and soul, and mind:"
So speaks to man that sacred word,
"With all thy heart;" no idol thing,
Though close around the heart it twine,
To darken that pure love of thine.
"With all thy mind;" each varied power,
And thoughts that glance behind, before,
"With soul and strength;" thy days of ease,
While vigor nerves each youthful limb,
And hope and joy, and health and peace,
All must be freely brought to him.

licence: Public domain: Emily Taylor died in 1872.
credits: Words by Emily Taylor (1795–1872), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
